tool_input.command: find src/test/java -iname "*ToString*" && echo --- && find src/test/java -name "*Test.java" | head -5 | xargs -I{} sh -c 'echo ==={}; head -30 {}'
tool_input.description: Find existing ToString tests and sample test class headers
Debug self-referencing array handling with a standalone test

result:
Wrote `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ToStringStyleAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 3 (`junit.framework.TestCase`) suite matching the project's existing style, covering setter/getter null-handling, defaults, `isFullDetail`, field start/end/separator logic, `removeLastFieldSeparator` edge cases, summary/detail appenders, primitive and array append overloads (including null arrays/elements and `arrayContentDetail`), cycle detection via the package-private registry, `appendStart`/`appendEnd`, `appendToString`/`appendSuper` boundary cases, and the documented output of all five predefined styles (`DEFAULT`, `NO_FIELD_NAMES`, `SHORT_PREFIX`, `SIMPLE`, `MULTI_LINE`).

58 of 59 tests pass. One test fails and shows a real bug:

- **`testAppendEndWithNullObjectIsConsistentWithAppendStart`** — `ToStringStyle.appendStart(buffer, null)` is null-safe and appends nothing, but `ToStringStyle.appendEnd(buffer, null)` still unconditionally appends the content-end marker (`"]"` for the default style) even though the object is `null`. This asymmetry means code that calls `appendStart`/`appendEnd` symmetrically around a possibly-null object gets unbalanced output (a trailing `]` with no matching opening bracket).
